title: How to invoke: pray God to give/free; ask Saints to take patronage and obtain from God—Miserere vs Ora pro nobis
source_text: LI. Atque haec quidem sunt quibus Scholae Romanae Doctores invocationem Sanctorum superstruunt. Caeterum quomodo Sancti sint invocandi, & quod discrimen sit inter invocationem illam, quam Deus sibi, ut propriam vindicat, & eam qua Sanctorum auxilium imploramus, sic exponit Catechismus ex Decreto Concilii Tridentini editus. Non enim, inquit, eodem modo Deum, & Sanctos ejus imploramus. Nam precamur Deum ut ipse vel bona det, vel liberet a malis; a Sanctis autem, quia gratiosi sunt apud Deum, petimus ut nostri patrocinium suscipiant, ut nobis a Deo impetrent ea quorum indigemus. Hinc duas adhibemus formulas modo differentes: ad Deum enim proprie dicimus, Miserere nobis, Audi nos; ad Sanctum, Ora pro nobis. Catech. Rom. part. 4. cap. 6. Sect. 1. num. 3.
pass_a_gloss: And these indeed are the things on which the Doctors of the Roman School build the invocation of the Saints. But how the Saints are to be invoked, and what discrimination there is between that invocation which God claims for Himself as proper, and that by which we implore the help of the Saints, the Catechism published from the Decree of the Council of Trent thus expounds. For we do not, it says, implore God and His Saints in the same way. For we pray God that He Himself either give goods or free from evils; but from the Saints, because they are gracious before God, we ask that they take up our patronage, that they obtain for us from God those things of which we are in need. Hence we employ two formulas differing in mode: for to God we properly say, Have mercy on us, Hear us; to a Saint, Pray for us. Roman Catechism, part 4, chapter 6, section 1, number 3.
pass_b_english: Trent Catechism: God and Saints are not asked the same way.
Ask God to give goods or free from evils; ask Saints, gracious before God, to take patronage and obtain from Him.
Formulas: to God ‘Have mercy / Hear us’; to a Saint ‘Pray for us.’
